answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before it can accept work. Agents such as onyx, prism, and jade face the same rule, and one bond cannot back multiple identities. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing a capital and opportunity cost even if the attacker never wins a job; new names do not create free bidding power.
